title: Benchmarking trigonometric continuous-variable gate primitives with trapped ions
authors: Tommaso Rainaldi, Jake Montgomery, Christopher G. Yale, Brian K. McFarland, Melissa C. Revelle, Daniel Lobser, Edward C. Tortorici, Susan Clark, George Siopsis, Matt Grau, Felix Ringer
abstract: Hybrid continuous-discrete-variable quantum processors can represent bosonic degrees of freedom directly in oscillator modes, or qumodes, while using qubits for control, readout, and nonlinear operations. Recently proposed trigonometric continuous-variable (CV) gate sets promote periodic functions of oscillator quadratures to elementary operations, making them natural primitives for compact variables, rotor models, lattice gauge theories, and anharmonic dynamics. Here we experimentally demonstrate and benchmark one-qumode cosine gates, and perform a mode-resolved marginal benchmark of two-qumode cosine-gate implementations, on the QSCOUT trapped-ion quantum platform. Our implementation uses collective motional modes of three- and four-ion $^{171}{\rm Yb}^{+}$ chains and realizes finite-step trigonometric-gate circuits through hybrid qubit-qumode operations and conditional phase-space displacements. In contrast to previous theoretical and compilation work, we focus on the gate-level characterization of the trigonometric primitives. We measure Fock-space transition probabilities, study their dependence on gate parameters and Trotter step number, and compare with simulations incorporating thermal initialization and motional dephasing. We also derive ideal gate matrix elements and phase-space diagnostics, connecting the measurements to the non-Gaussian structure generated by these gates. These results establish trigonometric CV gates as reusable building blocks for bosonic Hamiltonian simulations and hybrid quantum algorithms requiring intrinsically non-polynomial operations.
summary: The research experimentally benchmarks trigonometric continuous-variable quantum gates using trapped ions. By characterizing these elementary cosine gates at the level of individual operations, the authors demonstrate their utility as fundamental building blocks. This advances the feasibility of implementing complex bosonic simulations and hybrid quantum algorithms on current hardware platforms.
main_problem: The paper aims to experimentally benchmark trigonometric continuous-variable (CV) gate primitives, which are necessary for simulating complex bosonic dynamics.
main_result: Trigonometric CV gates are established as reusable building blocks for hybrid quantum algorithms and bosonic Hamiltonian simulations requiring non-polynomial operations.
method: The authors performed gate-level characterization by measuring Fock-space transition probabilities on the QSCOUT trapped-ion platform, comparing finite-step circuits against ideal evolution.
model_or_system: The physical system is a trapped-ion chain ($	ext{}^{171}	ext{Yb}^+$) utilizing collective motional modes (qumodes) alongside hyperfine states acting as qubits. The gates are implemented via hybrid qubit-qumode operations.
key_observables: Fock-space transition probabilities, Wigner function, Negativity, and Characteristic functions.
important_parameters: Gate parameters ($c$), Trotter step number, thermal initialization effects, and motional dephasing rates.
main_assumptions: The study compares finite-step circuit approximations against ideal trigonometric evolution while accounting for experimental imperfections like thermal noise and dephasing.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate measured detection probabilities for radial motional modes in three- and four-ion chains, relating to the implementation of collective motional gates.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from discussing CV-DV universality (Section II) to introducing the trapped-ion platform (Section III), analyzing ideal one- and two-qumode cosine gates using phase-space diagnostics (Section IV), detailing finite-step circuit realization (Section V), presenting experimental measurements (Section VI), and concluding (Section VII).
why_interesting: This work directly bridges advanced quantum information theory (CV gate sets) with state-of-the-art trapped-ion hardware, providing crucial empirical data on non-polynomial gates essential for simulating complex many-body physics.
